prepared_checkout_difference: none; the prepared branch was exactly at the recorded base commit
summary: The recorded base reproduces the missing public factory API. At the exact candidate commit, fresh ASGI apps hold distinct tokenizer/template/scheduler bindings in app state, request-scoped dispatch remains isolated under concurrent mounted-app traffic without changing the compatibility global, launch_server's single-tokenizer path constructs the served app with build_app, the focused regression suite passes, and a real Engine executes generation through the factory app on the assigned GPU. This is a full original-issue fix within the documented single-tokenizer in-process scope, not merely test hardening.

tests.what_was_measured: Original API availability; importing build_app and init_app_state raised ImportError as expected on the base.
Candidate regression and compatibility coverage: 31 tests and 12 subtests passed.

Independent concurrent isolation with two apps mounted under one parent. /model_info, /generate, and /v1/models all selected the correct app manager; all six requests returned 200; a conflicting legacy global remained unchanged; route counts matched the compatibility app.

A real prepared Engine was bound with build_app/init_app_state. /model_info returned 200 and /generate returned 200 with exactly eight completion tokens; two owned descendants were reaped after engine shutdown.

gpu_execution.evidence: AMD Instinct MI355X, gfx950, Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2, HIP 7.2.26015. The deterministic tiny Llama Engine generated output IDs [12, 100, 124, 43, 124, 43, 124, 51] with completion_tokens=8.

native_rebuilt_reason: The candidate changes Python serving code and tests only; repository-environment.json reports native=null and no native source or extension changed.
remaining_limitations: The public factory intentionally rejects tokenizer_worker_num != 1; multi-tokenizer worker bootstrap remains on the compatibility module app and shared-memory path.

SGLang runtime configuration namespaces remain process-wide, so separately bound apps in one process require compatible server configuration even though engine/tokenizer/template/scheduler request dispatch is isolated.

GPU qualification used one deterministic synthetic Llama on one AMD Instinct MI355X. It validates transport and engine execution, not semantic accuracy, other model architectures, multi-GPU, distributed, HTTP/2, TLS refresh, or native gRPC configurations.
No native code changed, so there was no rebuilt native library to validate.
